processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Produced a 39 kg low-density steel ingot with composition Fe-0.25C-3Mn-2Al-0.4Si-0.009S-0.009P.
Hot forged and cut into billets measuring 90 mm (length) × 70 mm (width) × 40 mm (thickness).
High-rigidity two-roll mill; six passes; yielding plates with final thickness 4 mm; finish rolling completed at 880 °C.
Four-roll reversible mill; resulting plate thickness 1.6 mm.
Annealed within the critical region (Ac1 705 °C, Ac3 950 °C) and air-cooled to room temperature; labeled AN800.
Aging in the lower bainite region refines bainitic structures and produces AN800-T; during tempering, carbon diffuses into austenite and more austenite is retained.

structures.overall_structure: Multiphase heterogeneous microstructure composed of ferrite (F), bainite/tempered martensite (B/TM), fresh martensite (FM) and retained austenite (RA); deformation-induced martensite (DIM) forms from RA during deformation.

microstructure_list.region: bulk annealed-and-aged microstructure (rolling plane/normal direction views)

phases_present.morphology: blocky/equiaxed ferrite grains decorated by B/TM, FM and RA
bainite/tempered martensite decorating ferrite grain boundaries

precipitates.distribution: carbides inside bainitic ferrite distributed at 60° angle to its boundaries; carbides randomly distributed in tempered martensite

defect_interactions.interaction_type: GND accumulation and back-stress generation at soft/hard domain interfaces
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: AN800-T has KAM_AVE = 0.69° (highest among the three samples); dislocations accumulate at grain boundaries and generate back stress.

interfaces.slip_behavior: Coordinated deformation between soft ferrite and hard domains: soft domain hardens while hard domain softens, maintaining deformation continuity and avoiding premature micro-porosity.
interfaces.phase_evolution: RA transforms into deformation-induced martensite (DIM) through the TRIP effect during deformation, enhancing strength and ductility.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Instron 3382 testing machine; load parallel to RD; DIC images captured every 2 s

comparative_performance.improvement_percentage: 2–3 times higher than conventional low-alloy high-strength steels
properties match those of advanced high-strength steels

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: etched with 4% nitric acid ethanol solution
characterization_methods.key_findings: AN800-T shows TM, FM, RA and B decorating ferrite grains (Fig. 2(g)).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 20 kV operating voltage; scanning step size 0.2 µm; TSL OIM 7.0; BCC and FCC indexed; minimum pixel size 9
characterization_methods.purpose: phase distribution, image quality (IQ) phase separation, and KAM strain analysis
characterization_methods.key_findings: AN800-T: FCC 0.024 / BCC 0.976; IQ FM 41 731.4; IQ B/TM 67 252.1; IQ histogram Peak I 46 517, Peak II 77 326, Ave 66 186; KAM_AVE = 0.69°.

characterization_methods.purpose: dislocation and substructure evolution; B/TM discrimination
characterization_methods.key_findings: AN800-T TEM shows TM and B regions (1 µm scale bar); carbide orientation distinguishes bainite from tempered martensite.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEOL JXA-8230 at 15 kV, working current 5 × 10^-8 A
characterization_methods.purpose: elemental distribution and phase composition quantification
characterization_methods.key_findings: In AN800-T, carbon is mainly concentrated in B/TM, FM and RA; phase compositions summarized in Table A1.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: accelerating voltage 40 kV; tube current 40 mA; scanning angle range 30°–110°
characterization_methods.key_findings: AN800-T XRD trace (Fig. 4(g)) shows BCC α peaks and weak γ (austenite) reflections.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: images captured every 2 s during tensile deformation
characterization_methods.key_findings: In AN800-T, two local strain concentration points are observed; as strain progresses they expand at a 45° angle and connect, leading to necking.

characterization_methods.technique: SEM dimple size statistics (Nano Measure software)
characterization_methods.key_findings: AN800-T dimple size: Ave = 1.44 µm, Peak I = 0.59 µm, Peak II = 2.14 µm; exhibits dimples plus some quasi-cleavage facets.

computational_details.simulation_method: Phase mechanical response model based on iso-work theory and the von Mises equivalent method
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Phases Ph = {F, B/TM, FM, RA, DIM}; iso-work assumption σ_F dε_F = σ_B/TM dε_B/TM = σ_FM dε_FM = σ_RA dε_RA = σ_DIM dε_DIM; RA transforms to DIM via TRIP effect.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated values align closely with experimental true stress-true strain data (Fig. 9(b)); the model overestimates at the initial stage of strain.

analytical_models.model_note: Eqs. (1)-(20); phase content of F, B/TM and FM remains constant during deformation; RA and DIM fractions are strain-dependent.
Eq. (3); fitted final DIM fraction for AN800-T = 1.16% (Fig. 7(b)).
Eq. (19); at necking strain the maximum stress caused by σ_B for AN800-T is 300 MPa; GND back-stress contribution is 291 MPa.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Reconstruction in three steps: optimizing orientation relationship, orientation coalescence, and regional voting between RA and DIM.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Final c for AN800-T determined as 0.15 µm.

unmapped_findings: Critical transformation temperatures of the experimental steel: Ac1 = 705 °C, Ac3 = 950 °C, Bf = 380 °C, Ms = 346 °C (source: b0149).
AN800-T phase composition from EPMA (Table A1, wt%): C 0.02(F)/0.35(B/TM)/0.57(FM)/1.20(RA)/1.20(DIM); Mn 2.70/2.80/3.00/3.80/3.80; Al 2/2/2/1.70/1.70; Si 0.40 in all phases (source: b0154).
After tensile fracture, AN800-T necking region austenite (RA) fraction = 0.004 and P-T-P_AVE = 4.48° (source: figure_012).
AN800-T dimple size statistics: Ave = 1.44 µm, Peak I = 0.59 µm, Peak II = 2.14 µm; fracture surface shows dimples plus some quasi-cleavage facets (source: figure_011, b0131).
At necking strain, B/TM contributed 41% of the flow stress in AN800-T; the maximum stress caused by back stress σ_B = 300 MPa and the GND back-stress contribution = 291 MPa (source: b0128, b0107).
Predicted final deformation-induced martensite (DIM) fraction for AN800-T = 1.16% (Fig. 7(b)); average DIM size c = 0.15 µm (source: figure_007, b0103).

The abstract reports the novel low-density steel with yield strength ≈1 000 MPa and elongation ≈18.7% (source: b0010); the measured AN800-T values are yield strength 985 MPa and elongation 18.7% (source: b0046).
